dossier.public_summary: The dip appears only in some TESS sectors and even disappears in one sector, with individual transits ranging from non-existent to unusually deep. This instability means the signal is not a repeating planet transit but a false alarm likely caused by measurement systematics on a spotted M dwarf.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 191.6% between sectors and is essentially ruled out as constant, well beyond calibration scatter.
The change is not between light-curve products but within the single QLP source, so it is a true astrophysical/systematic depth change, not a pipeline offset.

Individual transits are inconsistent: epoch -112 depth 12187 ppm vs epoch -57 depth -128 ppm (sigma -5.0), mean 6734 ppm with chi2 64.97 on 4 dof. Top three carry 0.987 of the SNR, with two near-zeroes and one highly unlikely deep event.
Signal essentially disappears in sector 34 and is twice the median in sector 8, as expected for a false alarm driven by pipeline/spot systematics rather than a stable planetary transit.
reasons.value: sector 8 12187 ppm, sector 34 -128 ppm, sector 61 6907 ppm, sector 88 6742 ppm

reasons.why: Independent scorer puts this at the 7th percentile for planets, consistent with the inconsistent transits and extreme sector depth change; flat-bottom shape alone cannot overcome this positive evidence against a planet.
